meeting.title: Spokane Chiefs <> Salesforce/Mulesoft: Pacolon integration financial discussion

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Last week, I just got shifted a little bit and then... Our entire leadership team was out, so I just tried to give them at least the information. Then I had a photo with them yesterday, and they had a couple of questions just to make sure that we were all on the same page.
Then we are working through the budget right now and trying to get that full amount in there. Only did meet with Packy Owen and what they were suggesting was not what we were looking for as far as their implementation.
So as of right now, we would still go with Dataskate and everything to get that all set up there just because of the way that they were explaining it. We'd have to work with Salesforce anyway on getting all their data. They'd pretty much take all the data that we'd have, right? When it happens, they'll be able to send us that data.
But we would have to figure out how to configure that data in Salesforce. So with that just being an extra layer, it makes no sense for us to do. But as far as the Mulesoft software, I know originally, and again, trying to just make sure that we're understanding it correctly. The $19,500 is for the software itself. There's no more starter or substarter pack, it's just straight-up Mulesoft as the software.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Correct? Correct.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Yeah. Okay. And then the implementation of the 14000. That's just the first year to get it all set up and everything to get the actual process started correct. And it's that's just it's not going to be a reoccurring charge every year.
It's just the one time set up.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Yeah, it's a one-time setup and not for the whole year, Brandon. It's for the number of weeks that we've mentioned to complete the project.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Two.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: So assuming let's. Once the project is done, then I think we will hand it over to you. For you to kind of take over.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Once we get to that point too, part of Mulesoft comes with premier success. So as you guys do, maybe think, "Okay, we want to connect Next. We or whatever else down the line." If you do want to reach out to us and get any best practices, that's part of what comes with your package. We'll set up a coaching session. You don't have to pay for that either.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Then okay, that was one of the questions that they had. So appreciate that. Then obviously, the renewal credit is just paying off or getting reimbursed for because our original time was in October.
So from their standpoint, they again just want to make sure that from the ticket staff, we're actually using this and implementing. Note talking to David, our accounting team isn't quite ready to make the jump into connecting the systems. At any point, if we do end up wanting to...
I know you said that there isn't like an API set amount. You can't do multiple APIs. It's just Mulesoft. Would the implementation just be like, "Hey, we want to add this on if it's another 14,000 that one year?" Are we able to add without having to increase the cost of Mulesoft? Or is it like, "Hey, this price is just for the one connection?"

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: That's a great question. It would be more the former, right? So since it's like a purely consumption metric, whatever's left over from this first project put towards the net suite. Totally fine. That's exactly how we want people using it. The whole point is that you get cheaper than more projects that you're doing okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Or because when we started talking about that, they were like, "Okay, well, now we're getting away from that and they. And we just want to make sure that we're like, "Hey, we could add this on if we feel comfortable adding it in."
We just play for the implementation. So that works out really well for us. Yeah, the leadership being out last week wasn't ideal because we had three meetings set up with them and then again default with them yesterday. They're still trying to dive in and make it work in the budget. We just got to make sure that because we are almost doubling our cost, especially for year one, we are more than doubling it. They just want to make sure that we have the actual case study into how we're actually going to make it work perfectly.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: He.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Brandon, sorry I hopped on late. I'm not trying to be creepy. I'm driving. That's why my camera's off. But great to see you. Sorry, you... I walked into you talking at the beginning. You said you wanted to make sure it's put to use immediately. Do you mind just repeating that part of it?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
More so that I know it's going to take a couple of months to get the whole thing set up. But just like once we have the connection made and we're all comfortable with it, we want to make sure that we hit the ground running.
So once our home opener goes and those leases and everything gets put into Salesforce that we're not just waiting on them like we typically have done. We're actually able to show from year one the return of this taking place right away, not waiting until midway through the season to start getting through everything.
So from a leadership standpoint, they just want to make sure that we're actually when we're increasing $20,000, that we're actually putting that to good use and not just using it to make our job easier. In a sense.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Totally. Do you feel like you guys have the bandwidth to implement it on the timeline that they're asking for? Obviously, with Dataskate Health...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
We do. We've kind of changed our calendars. Even so, the reason why I'm the only one here is because the other two guys, Marcus and Craig, are both out. So we've tried to kind of push our vacations to June and July, and that way in August, when we have kind of everything kind of set up with Kailash, that we can actually start running through everything and making sure that if they're hey, this doesn't look exactly what we're looking for. We can either make those adjustments and we're all going to be in the office at that point. Compared to moving around in like Hege, people are only in the office.
Say, like, we need to have all eyes on this. We'll all kind of be there together.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Okay? Okay, awesome. And obviously, we appreciate you rearranging like your PTO that's obviously a lot, so thank you for doing that. What do you think is, like, the path to actually getting, like, pen to paper? What approvals are you waiting on? When do you think those conversations can happen? Et cetera.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
So we're working through the budget as of we speak. Pretty much has to be set quote unquote. Just because our fiscal year started July 1st. By the end of this month, there was a little hiccup last week with our leadership team. One of their family members passed away, so they were away from all that, and then that left the other people in leadership to go with them to the memorial service and everything.
So we were out two days last week from that, but I would say by the middle part of next week, if we don't have an answer for you, then I'm not doing my part. I've pretty much finalized our side of the budget, and it's really just trying to find from the expense standpoint because we have to get new hockey equipment.
If we can find room in there and be like, "Hey, this is why it's going to cost this much money." We should be able to take this on. We have room in the capital budget because we just paid off quite a bit of that.
So hopefully, that can just get moved over there. But by next Wednesday, if I don't have an answer for Sam, David, or Michelle, then I'm not doing my part here.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Well, we appreciate you, Brand, and thank you for doing that. Yeah. I'm so sorry to hear about the death in the family. That's obviously really tough. So glad everybody was able to get to the memorial service.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I started... Sam, when I was emailing me, I was like, "Hey, this isn't going to work anymore. Is there any way we just thinking?" I was like a couple of hours prior because they were like, "Hey, we really don't want to try to rush anything." I was like, "Yeah, I'm not trying to push this any further than that." Will.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
Totally, that's one of those things that it's like, "Okay, we're going to take a break for a second." Okay, sweet. Well, that sounds like a plan. Yeah, I'm mostly asking when you think you can get in front of them to basically finalize everything.
Because, obviously, as we know, with summer, people take PTO, so I don't know if they're going back out toward the back half of the month. So the more we can try to get this signed by the end of next week...
I think that's probably in everyone's best interest.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Then the one thing I just wanted to make sure... I know we talked about it a couple of weeks ago. I believe... So with our fiscal year starting July 1st, our accounting team really likes to have the billing and everything done after July 1st.
So if we were to put pen and paper next week, is there still a way to get the billing paid starting in July instead of having it right in there?

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Yes. So what we would do is add language to the contract that essentially is called pre-build day one. What that means is let's assume that we do a July 15th start date. So it gives Kailash two weeks to get resources aligned, etc. Then we would have it so the bill doesn't drop until the start date of the contract, and it's not due until 30 days after that.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Yeah, cool, easy enough.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah. I think the only other piece for that is I think we did talk about big quarterly billing too, so we could do that or annual, whatever you guys want.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay, perfect. I'll let our accounting team know that they know that. So that'll help break things up, too.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: If needed. Yeah, it can usually be nice to, you know, par parcel things out, or maybe all at once, different strokes for different folks. Always good to have the option. Cool. I guess maybe unless there's anything else, maybe we could touch base, like early next week or later this week, I guess. Brand. What do you. What do you. What do you think's best for us here?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
If we could set something up for next Monday or Tuesday, that'd be perfect. Afternoon is preferred. Right now, we have a ton of meetings in the morning just going over budget. So that way we can readjust in the afternoon.
But if you have something open next Monday or Tuesday afternoon, that would work really well for me.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Monday at 1 pm or Tuesday at 1:30 or 2:30. All seem good for my end.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Could we do the Tuesday at 1:30? Yep, we're all free then.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Perfect, I'll move the invite to then. Yeah, and then if any questions or anything come up in the meantime, obviously feel free to reach out. We'll keep getting our ducks in a row on our end here, and yeah, looking forward to getting this one kicked off.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Thank you, Sam.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Question... Thank you, thanks.
Take care.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Bye.
